newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Gibraltar seeks EU help against Spain.
newsitem.headline: Gibraltar seeks EU help against Spain.

text.p: Gibraltar launched a campaign in Brussels on Tuesday to get European Union help against what it sees as Spanish discrimination in areas from aviation to the movement of people.

Officials from the British colony's government, including Chief Minister Peter Caruna, were to meet for talks with members of the European Parliament and European Commission to air their grievances against Madrid.
Spain claims sovereignty over Gibraltar, a tiny pensinsular on its southern tip that was ceded to Britain by the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713.
At a briefing for reporters, Caruna said Gibraltar's 30,000 citizens wanted to take their full role in the European Union, but were being prohibited from doing so.

"The reality of the matter is that Spain not only actively seeks Gibraltar's exclusion from crucial (EU) measures, but conducts her relationship with Gibraltar as if we were not an intrinsic part of the (Union)," he said.
Caruna cited long checks at the border, a veto against the colony being included in EU air liberalisation, and attempts to exclude it from EU directives relating to the free movement of people.
Gibraltar's people are European Union citizens through their links to Britain although the colony is exempted from some EU rules.

Caruna noted that Gibraltarians were not permitted to vote in European Parliament elections, which he described as "a clear breach of the principles of the (EU's) Treaty of Rome which call for universal suffrage."
